notes: Read all four target units, full nuclear-energy context, all twenty-four candidates and the review. Disposed candidates one through nine because they import nuclear assertions from preceding context while citing the renewables unit. Corrected evidence for the renewable and grid claims to their actual units, named solar and wind rather than these sources, and restored U.S. scope to the coal-policy positions. Restored the concession that alternative fuels will shape the U.S. energy future.

claims.claim_text: Alternative power sources must enter the U.S. energy mainstream.
Solar-energy technology had improved significantly in recent years.
Commercial wind-power development promises major cost and environmental-protection benefits.
Support for solar, wind, geothermal and hydropower energy.
Technological development is expected to increase solar, wind and other alternative energy sources' economic viability.
Support for a long-term energy tax credit applying equally to all renewable power sources.
Support for modernizing the U.S. electricity grid to give American consumers and businesses more affordable and reliable power.
Commitment to unleash innovation so entrepreneurs develop technologies for a more advanced, robust U.S. transmission system meeting growing energy demand.
Alternative fuels are expected to shape the U.S. energy future.
Coal must remain a major component of U.S. energy independence because it is characterized as a strategic national resource.
No U.S. strategy for reducing energy costs is considered viable without continued coal production and use.
